title: Abaye Kashisha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Shabbat 56a mentions him setting two statements of Rav against one another. Hyman suggests that the Abaye reporting Rav in Shabbat 57b may be Abaye Kashisha. He recites baraitot in Yevamot 24a and Ketubot 94a; in Ketubot 96b he gives Rabbi Yose’s parable beginning “What is this like?” Sanhedrin 7a preserves his saying: “A quarrel is like the planking of a bridge: once it is fixed, it stays fixed.”

notes.text: Rami is not a new speaker: the opening describes setting Rav’s statements against each other. The final proverb concerns a quarrel, not a merchant. Rashi explains the bridge-plank image as a quarrel becoming entrenched through repetition.
